blogs.title: From Canine Bite to Complement Crisis
blogs.description: Capnocytophaga canimorsus is an uncommon but high‑mortality zoonotic pathogen that can evolve from a simple dog bite into a fulminant sepsis cascade culminating in complement‑mediated thrombotic microangiopathy (CM‑HUS). This post reviews the epidemiology and pathophysiological mechanisms that enable this fastidious gram‑negative rod to activate the alternative complement pathway in susceptible adults, the clinical red flags that should prompt early suspicion after animal exposure, and how rapid molecular diagnostics such as real‑time nanopore sequencing can shorten time to identification compared with conventional culture.

blogs.title: When Sepsis Feels Like TTP – Distinguishing TMAs in Critical Illness
blogs.description: Severe sepsis frequently produces pancytopenia and coagulation abnormalities that mimic thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP). We dissect the laboratory cues that help clinicians differentiate between TTP and CM‑HUS—ADAMTS13 activity thresholds (<10% versus >10%), PLASMIC scores, schistocyte prevalence versus diffuse intravascular coagulation—and discuss when plasma exchange is truly life‑saving versus merely temporizing.

blogs.title: Beyond C3/C4 – Interpreting Complement Function During Atypical HUS
blogs.description: Atypical HUS often surprises clinicians because routine complement panels (C3/C4) remain normal amidst aggressive endothelial injury. This piece explains how functional assays (e.g., AH50 for alternative pathway activity), factor levels (H, I, B), and anti‑factor H antibody tests provide a deeper view than static protein levels, especially when patients are undergoing plasma exchange or terminal complement blockade.

blogs.title: Putting Eculizumab on Hold? Navigating Complement Inhibition During Active Bacterial Sepsis
blogs.description: Initiating terminal‐pathway blockade with eculizumab during ongoing bacteremia poses an inherent risk against encapsulated organisms like C.~canimorsus. We outline a stepwise decision tree—from timing blood culture clearance, through vaccination strategies (Menveo/Bexsero), prophylactic penicillin regimens, to close infectious monitoring—that balances rapid TMA control against infective vulnerability.

blogs.title: From DIC to MAHA – A Dynamic Clinical Trajectory in Sepsis‑Triggered TMA
blogs.description: This article follows one patient’s journey from septic shock with disseminated intravascular coagulation through newfound isolated hemolysis and persistent thrombocytopenia after initial improvement—a classic “delayed” onset of thrombotic microangiopathy. We propose practical monitoring checkpoints (daily CBC morphology and haptoglobin checks) and highlight how re‑evaluation at this juncture can catch late‑emerging hemolysis before irreversible organ damage ensues.
